steps.title: Import React and useRef from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useRef hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useRef from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useRef from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useRef is added, making them available for use in the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the useRef hook. This is the foundation for using React's imperative handle capabilities.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useRef from the 'react' package using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React and useRef from 'react' using an import statement.

steps.title: Import useImperativeHandle from 'react'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for the useImperativeHandle hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: You need to import useImperativeHandle from the same package you imported React and useRef from.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a hook from 'react'
import { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have both useRef and useImperativeHandle imported from 'react'.
successCriteria: The import statement includes useImperativeHandle from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported useImperativeHandle from 'react'. This hook will allow you to customize the instance value exposed when using refs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but check the import syntax. Make sure you're importing useImperativeHandle from 'react' using the same pattern as useRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import useImperativeHandle from 'react' using the same import statement pattern as useRef.

steps.title: Create a forwardRef component called ChildComponent
steps.instruction: Create a child component named ChildComponent using React.forwardRef. The component should accept props and a ref as parameters, but you don't need to implement the body yet.
steps.hint: Use React.forwardRef to create a component that can receive a ref from its parent. The forwardRef function takes a callback with (props, ref) parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a ChildComponent defined using React.forwardRef with props and ref parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a forwardRef component. This allows ChildComponent to receive a ref from its parent component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using React.forwardRef and that the component accepts both props and ref parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a component called ChildComponent using React.forwardRef that accepts props and ref as parameters.

steps.title: Add TypeScript interface for ChildComponent props
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'ChildComponentProps' for the props of your ChildComponent. The interface can be empty initially (no properties).
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and empty curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: An empty interface named 'ChildComponentProps' is defined, ready to have props added in future steps.
successCriteria: The interface must be named 'ChildComponentProps' and must be defined with empty curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TypeScript interface for ChildComponent props. This provides type safety for the component's props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined an interface named 'ChildComponentProps' with empty curly braces. Check your syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't defined correctly. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword followed by 'ChildComponentProps' and empty curly braces {}.

steps.title: Add TypeScript interface for the exposed methods
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'ChildHandle' that defines a method called 'focus' which returns 'void'. This interface will describe the methods that the parent component can call on the child component via the forwarded ref.
steps.hint: Define an interface with a single method signature: 'focus(): void'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a new TypeScript interface named 'ChildHandle' with a 'focus' method signature.
successCriteria: The code must include a TypeScript interface named 'ChildHandle' with a method 'focus' that returns 'void'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TypeScript interface for the methods that will be exposed via useImperativeHandle. This provides type safety for the parent component when calling methods on the child ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you've created an interface named 'ChildHandle' with a 'focus' method that returns 'void'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't created correctly. You need to define a TypeScript interface named 'ChildHandle' with a method called 'focus' that returns 'void'.

steps.title: Add input element inside ChildComponent
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildComponent's return statement, add an input element with type='text'.
steps.hint: The input element should be a self-closing JSX tag: <input type="text" />.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent now contains an input element that will later be controlled via imperative methods.
successCriteria: The code includes an <input type="text" /> element inside ChildComponent's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the input element that will serve as the target for imperative control.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added an <input> element with type='text' inside the ChildComponent's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing. Add <input type="text" /> inside ChildComponent's return statement.

steps.title: Create a ref for the input element
steps.instruction: Inside the ChildComponent function body (before the return statement), create a ref for the input element using useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null). Name this ref 'inputRef'.
steps.hint: Call useRef with the generic type HTMLInputElement and initial value null, then assign it to a constant variable named inputRef.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent now has a ref object called inputRef that will be used to reference the input element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref for the input element using useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null). This ref will allow you to access the DOM input element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct syntax: const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null). Check that you've included the HTMLInputElement type and initialized with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref wasn't created correctly. Inside ChildComponent, you need to call useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null) and assign it to a variable named inputRef.

steps.title: Implement useImperativeHandle in ChildComponent
steps.instruction: Inside the ChildComponent, call useImperativeHandle with the ref parameter and a function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: useImperativeHandle takes two arguments: the ref and a function that returns the object to expose. Place this call at the top of the component body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useImperativeHandle hook is called with ref and a function returning an empty object, establishing the foundation for exposing methods.
successCriteria: The code includes a call to useImperativeHandle with ref as the first argument and a function returning an object as the second argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly implemented useImperativeHandle with the ref parameter and a function returning an object. This sets up the structure for exposing custom methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useImperativeHandle with exactly two arguments: the ref parameter and a function that returns an object (even if empty).
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires calling useImperativeHandle inside the ChildComponent. Remember to use the ref parameter and provide a function that returns an object.

steps.title: Define focus method in useImperativeHandle
steps.instruction: Inside the useImperativeHandle call, define a focus method that calls inputRef.current?.focus() to expose this functionality to the parent component.
steps.hint: Add a focus property to the object returned from useImperativeHandle that contains a function calling the input element's focus method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useImperativeHandle hook now exposes a focus method that can be called from the parent component to focus the input element.
successCriteria: The useImperativeHandle callback returns an object
The object contains a focus property
The focus property is a function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a focus method that will expose the input's focus functionality to the parent component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the focus method properly calls inputRef.current?.focus() and is defined inside the useImperativeHandle callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The focus method wasn't properly defined. Check that you're returning an object with a focus property that calls inputRef.current?.focus() inside the useImperativeHandle callback.

steps.title: Create ParentComponent
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component called ParentComponent. It should be a function component that returns a JSX element (you can start with an empty div).
steps.hint: Define a function named ParentComponent that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ParentComponent function is defined, ready to be used as the parent component.
successCriteria: The code includes a function or arrow function named ParentComponent that returns JSX (e.g., a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ParentComponent. This will be the component that uses the child's exposed methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named ParentComponent that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ParentComponent hasn't been created yet. Create a function component named ParentComponent that returns JSX.

steps.title: Create ref for ChildComponent in ParentComponent
steps.instruction: Inside the ParentComponent, create a ref using useRef that will reference the ChildComponent. The ref should be typed to match the ExposedMethods interface and initialized with null.
steps.hint: Use the useRef hook with the ExposedMethods type as the generic parameter. Initialize it with null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a typed ref in a parent component
const parentRef = useRef<ExposedMethods>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent now has a ref that can be used to access methods exposed by the ChildComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed ref in the parent component that will allow you to access the child's exposed methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the ExposedMethods type for the ref and initializing it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside ParentComponent, create a ref using useRef<ExposedMethods>(null).

steps.title: Add button to trigger child's focus method
steps.instruction: Inside the ParentComponent's return statement, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls childRef.current?.focus() to trigger the child input's focus method.
steps.hint: Add <button onClick={() => childRef.current?.focus()}>Focus Child Input</button> inside the ParentComponent's JSX, after the ChildComponent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent now has a button that, when clicked, will call the focus method exposed by the ChildComponent via useImperativeHandle, focusing the child's input element.
successCriteria: Add a button element inside ParentComponent's return JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that triggers the child's exposed focus method. This completes the useImperativeHandle pattern where the parent can call specific methods on the child component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a button element with an onClick handler that calls childRef.current?.focus(). Check that the button is inside the ParentComponent's return statement and the onClick handler uses the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button to trigger the child's focus method is missing or incorrect. You need to add a button element with an onClick handler that calls childRef.current?.focus() inside the ParentComponent's return statement.
